When nitriles (compounds containing the -C≡N functional group) react with acids, especially non-oxidizing acids, one of the main hazards is the potential generation of hydrogen cyanide (HCN), which is a highly toxic gas. Nitriles can undergo hydrolysis in acidic conditions, which can lead to the formation of HCN.

Hydrogen cyanide is extremely toxic even in small amounts and can cause rapid death by inhibiting cellular respiration. This makes the reaction between nitriles and acids particularly dangerous due to the potential for toxic gas generation.
